title: get_changes_since for messages: no early-exit when since_version >= current_version
description: MessageStore::get_changes_since does not have the early-exit guard that ChatStore::get_changes_since and ContactStore::get_changes_since both have (the since_counter >= current_counter check). It runs the SQL query unconditionally. This means that if a client sends a sinceState equal to the current state, a query still runs and returns empty. This is not a behavioral bug (the SQL WHERE clause is correct) but it means the two faster stores (chat, contact) have a microoptimization path that messages lack. However, the real issue: get_changes_since does not validate that since_version is not in the future (> current). A client with a state token from a future state (malformed or from a different instance) gets an empty result instead of cannotCalculateChanges. ChatStore and ContactStore explicitly check since_counter >= current_counter and short-circuit — they use the resolved current state to gate. MessageStore skips this check. For a since_version larger than current, the SQL query returns empty correctly by accident, but the returned new_state will be the current state, not an error — so the client will stop retrying thinking it is up to date.
